A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same work by Bal and Sengupta. S6 in v1 maps to P-SpikeSSM in v2, and the methods, results, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report original classification results on psMNIST, SC10 and five LRA tasks, spiking-activity analyses and accuracy statistics from randomly seeded runs.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark results and reports additional component ablations, neuron-count experiments, and accuracy and timing comparisons with an implemented LIF variant.

M1.justification: V2 extends the clipping operation to sigma(z) = clamp(az+b) and explicitly evaluates learning its parameters. It also corrects the written spike-sampling inequality, without establishing a corresponding implementation change. SpikeMixer and FuseClamp largely rename and formalize v1's existing mixer, residual, normalization and clipping operations; the underlying SSM and expectation surrogate remain.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate psMNIST, raw SC10 audio and the same five LRA tasks: ListOps, Text, Retrieval, Image and Pathfinder. V2 moves dataset descriptions into Appendix C. Its added ablations vary model components and sizes within existing coverage.

E2.justification: The LRA comparison adds BinaryS4D, FLASH-quad and Transnormer T2, while removing Longformer, Reformer, Synthesizer, BigBird, Performer and Luna-256. The psMNIST table drops TrellisNet and HiPPO-LegS; SC10 drops the LipschitzRNN failure entry. Section 4.1.2 additionally compares against an implemented SSM-plus-LIF variant, substantially changing the comparison evidence.

E3.justification: The retained split descriptions and task-specific hyperparameters match, including v1 Table S2 and v2 Table S1. V2 adds controlled component experiments, a two-layer neuron-count sweep and training/inference timing comparisons. It replaces normalized-OPS energy estimation with an explicit 45nm, 32-bit operation-cost calculation against S4, using standard convolution and separate input/output firing rates.

E4.justification: V2 adds tests of surrogate necessity, neuron mixing, normalization removal, fixed versus learnable sigma, neuron population size, and stochastic versus LIF spike generation. These directly examine component utility and computational bottlenecks, questions largely untested in v1. Conversely, v1's Appendix Figure S1 train/validation/test convergence analysis is removed; the sparsity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V2 removes v1 Table S1's seven-task accuracy statistics with ± values and Appendix C's disclosure of ten randomly seeded instances per experiment. It also drops the activity figure caption's statement that results cover 20 runs. This substantially reduces uncertainty and repetition reporting; it does not establish that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: From v1 Table 3 to v2 Table 2, reported accuracies change for ListOps from 55.70 to 58.20, Text 77.62 to 81.20, Retrieval 88.48 to 88.53, Image 80.10 to 80.60, and Pathfinder 83.41 to 84.80. These revised results accompany the method extension; psMNIST 98.4 and SC10 95.6 remain unchanged. V2 adds ablation, baseline and timing outcomes and removes convergence and accuracy-statistics entries. The energy estimate changes from approximately 30× to over 70× under a different calculation.

T1.justification: The convolution derivation and HiPPO/kernel-computation arguments in Appendices A-B remain substantively unchanged. V2 introduces the affine-clamp definition, corrects the Bernoulli sampling inequality so it agrees with E[St] = ps[t], and replaces the normalized-OPS equations with explicit operation-count energy expressions. These are limited mathematical revisions without a new theorem or substantial proof.

C1.justification: The central claims of effective long-range classification, parallel training and sparse-spiking efficiency remain. V2's introduction qualifies its LRA benchmark claim as applying to fully spiking models and explicitly claims elimination of additional simulation time steps used by spiking transformers. Its stronger emphasis on named architectural blocks mostly reframes contributions already present in v1.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive arguments about LIF layers creating sequential bottlenecks after SSMs and interprets the new component ablations. It discusses normalization's deployment tradeoff and the accuracy/computation tradeoff of learnable sigma. It qualifies v1's broad accumulation-only account by acknowledging multiplication costs and explicitly limits the energy analysis through approximations and architectural omissions. The specific generative-task future-work discussion is dropped.

D1.justification: V2 specifies the existing residual-addition, batch-normalization and clipping sequence, identifies pooling in the decoder, and supplies per-layer firing rates and runtime measurements. Hardware, task-specific hyperparameters, discretization range and memory figures are retained. A new reproducibility ambiguity appears: Section 3.1 specifies a=1, b=0 for direct clipping, whereas Section 4.1.2 reverses those values.

R1.justification: V2 substantially repositions the work against SSM-plus-LIF approaches, adding Stan and Rhodes/BinaryS4D and expanding discussion of Du et al. around real-valued inputs, sequential processing and computational efficiency. It removes the earlier alternative-neuron survey and associated stochastic-neuron and dynamic-threshold references, while adding relevant transformer, SSM, SpikeGPT and hardware-sampling literature.

P1.justification: The title and model terminology change, and the abstract, introduction and contribution narrative are extensively rewritten. Methodology is reorganized around SpikeSampler and architectural blocks, with the LIF discussion moved after the proposed formulation. Dataset descriptions and memory discussion move to appendices, and experimentation is consolidated into results, ablations and energy analysis.

P2.justification: V2 combines the earlier architecture and retained sparsity graphics into Figure 1, replaces the LIF comparison schematic with a temporal computation-flow diagram, and adds the neuron-count plot and ablation table. It removes the convergence figure and accuracy-statistics table, restructures the LRA table including dropping its average column, and substantially changes typography and figure/table placement.

improvement.justification: V2's component ablations, LIF timing comparison and BinaryS4D baseline address important gaps in v1's evidence for component utility and efficiency. However, removing the ten-seed accuracy summaries weakens support for revised LRA results, and conflicting fixed-sigma settings make a new comparison less reproducible. The expanded energy analysis is more explicit but remains approximate under changed assumptions. These substantive benefits and losses leave the net direction of overall quality uncertain.
